He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]]. ==Early life== Bassey was born in [[Lagos]], Nigeria, where he played [[association football|soccer]] until age 12, standing {{convert|6|ft|1|in|m|2}} at the time.{{cite web |last1=Estes |first1=Gentry |title=How one of the nation's top 2019 prospects, Charles Bassey, ended up playing in Louisville |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/02/14/charles-bassey-2019-basketball-prospect-aspire-academy-louisville/327799002/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=February 14, 2018}} At that age, he was discovered by a youth [[basketball]] coach while Bassey was selling [[fried chicken]] on the side of a road and wearing [[flip-flops]] that were too small for him.{{cite web |last1=Rosser |first1=Evan |title=All Access: In Africa with Raptors GM Masai Ujiri |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/big-read-giant-steps-masai-ujiri-giants-of-africa/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=October 11, 2015}}{{cite web |title=Charles Bassey: From Selling Fried Chicken In Nigeria At Age 12 To Top Prospect In Four Years |url=http://www.lex18.com/story/34215173/charles-bassey-from-selling-fried-chicken-in-nigeria-at-age-12-to-top-prospect-in-four-years |publisher=[[WLEX-TV|lex18]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=January 9, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618232811/http://www.lex18.com/story/34215173/charles-bassey-from-selling-fried-chicken-in-nigeria-at-age-12-to-top-prospect-in-four-years |archive-date=June 18, 2018 |url-status=dead }} He stopped playing soccer soon after, instead focusing on developing his basketball skills. At age 14, Bassey was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of basketball camp Giants of Africa, a program established by [[Toronto Raptors]] executive [[Masai Ujiri]].{{cite web |last1=Hickman |first1=Jason |title=6-foot-10 Nigerian import Charles Bassey could be high school basketball's best freshman |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/OMSa5fcCQUeU-Z2-xxVbTQ/video-photos--6-foot-10-nigerian-import-charles-bassey-could-be-high-school-basketball%E2%80%99s-best-freshman.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=November 20, 2015}} ==High school career== At age 14, Bassey stood {{convert|6|ft|10|in|m|2}} and moved to the United States to continue his basketball career at [[St. Anthony Catholic High School]], a [[private school]] in [[San Antonio|San Antonio, Texas]].{{cite web |last1=Hille |first1=Bob |title=5-star C Charles Bassey commits to WKU, reclassifies to class of 2018 |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/charles-bassey-western-kentucky-5-star-center-commits-reclassifies-2018/1m66gxyf4cckf1v8jl85tntac4 |publisher=[[Sporting News]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=June 14, 2018}} By then, recruiting analysts considered him one of the best prospects in his class.{{cite web |last1=Burlison |first1=Frank |title=My Top 35, and more, Pangos Frosh/Soph wrap-up |url=http://www.burlisononbasketball.com/2015/11/charles-bassey-tops-pangos-all-froshsoph-selections/ |publisher=Burlison on Basketball |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=November 12, 2015}}{{cite web |last1=Harvey |first1=Buck |title=The next Shaq? Road runs through San Antonio again |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/columnists/buck_harvey/article/The-next-Shaq-Road-runs-through-San-Antonio-again-6603166.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=October 31, 2015}} As a freshman, Bassey averaged 20.2 points, 17.1 rebounds and 5.9 blocks per game, leading his team to the [[Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools]] (TAPPS) title game.{{cite web |last1=Harris |first1=Don |title=Move over Shaq, meet San Antonio's next basketball superstar |url=http://news4sanantonio.com/sports/high-school/move-over-shaq-meet-san-antonios-next-basketball-superstar |publisher=[[WOAI-TV]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=February 26, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=Ticket to the top |url=https://www.expressnews.com/st-anthony-basketball-ticket-to-top/ |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=June 23, 2017}} Bassey competed in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game, where he was named MVP.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=Nigerian Charles Bassey makes up for late start, lifts Black team in International game at Jordan Classic |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/charles-bassey-r-j-barrett-montverde-academy-st-anthony-jordan-brand-classic |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=April 15, 2016}} Before his sophomore season, Bassey was ruled ineligible by the TAPPS, with St. Anthony filing an appeal.{{cite web |last1=Bossi |first1=Eric |title=Nation's top sophomore Charles Bassey ruled ineligible |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/nation-s-top-sophomore-charles-bassey-ruled-ineligible |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=November 17, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=St. Anthony names ineligible players, awaits response from TAPPS |url=https://blog.mysanantonio.com/hssports/2016/11/boys-basketball-st-anthony-names-ineligible-players-awaits-response-from-tapps/ |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=November 18, 2016}} He still made his season debut, and head coach Jeff Merritt was fired for playing an ineligible player.{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=St. Anthony fires coach for playing ineligible Bassey |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/high_school/high_school_basketball/article/St-Anthony-fires-coach-for-playing-ineligible-10659843.php?t=f40935eb0fbc83a41f |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=December 1, 2016}} St. Anthony withdrew from the TAPPS and joined the Texas Christian Athletic League, allowing Bassey to become eligible again.{{cite web |last1=Marquez |first1=RJ |title=Charles Bassey, other players now eligible as St. Anthony HS leaves TAPPS |url=https://www.ksat.com/sports/charles-bassey-other-ineligible-players-to-return-as-st-anthony-hs-leaves-tapps |publisher=[[KSAT-TV|KSAT]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=December 6, 2016}} For his junior season, Bassey transferred to [[DeSales High School (Louisville, Kentucky)|DeSales High School]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky]] and began playing basketball for Aspire Basketball Academy in Louisville. He made the decision after Hennssy Auriantal, his [[legal guardian]] and an assistant coach at St. Anthony, was dismissed from the program.{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=St. Anthony coach Hennssy Auriantal dismissed after Charles Bassey controversy |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/high_school/high_school_basketball/article/St-Anthony-coach-Hennssy-Auriantal-dismissed-11342319.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=July 25, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=Boys basketball: Aspire Academy introduces former St. Anthony players |url=https://blog.mysanantonio.com/hssports/2017/08/boys-basketball-aspire-academy-introduces-former-st-anthony-players/ |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=August 26, 2017}} As a junior, he averaged 19.4 points and 12.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Charles Bassey commits to Western Kentucky, reclassifies to 2018 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23785371/charles-bassey-commits-western-kentucky-hilltoppers-reclassifies-2018 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=June 13, 2018}} ===Recruiting=== Bassey was a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top [[center (basketball)|centers]] in the 2018 class. On June 13, 2018, he reclassified to the 2018 class and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers men's basketball|Western Kentucky]]. {{College athlete recruit start|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Charles Bassey | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Lagos|Lagos, Nigeria]] | highschool = Aspire Academy (KY) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 220 | 40 = | commitdate = June 13, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 92 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Western Kentucky 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers Recruiting Class | 247 school = | rivals school = westernkentucky | scout s = | espn schoolid = 98 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 9 | 247 overall = 9 | espn overall = 18 | accessdate = January 14, 2018 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 18, 2018, Bassey recorded a freshman season-high 25 points and 10 rebounds in a 78–62 loss to [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]].{{cite web |title=UCF beats WKU 78-62 for Myrtle Beach title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401096897 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=November 18, 2018}} On January 31, 2019, he posted 22 points and 18 rebounds, the most rebounds by a Western Kentucky freshman since 1972.{{cite web |title=Surging Bassey Wins Sixth C-USA Freshman of the Week Award |url=https://wkusports.com/news/2019/2/4/mens-basketball-surging-bassey-wins-sixth-c-usa-freshman-of-the-week-award.aspx |website=Western Kentucky University Athletics |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=February 4, 2019}} As a freshman, Bassey averaged 14.6 points, 10 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game, earning First Team All-[[Conference USA]], Defensive Player of the Year and Freshman of the Year honors. He recorded the most rebounds, blocks and [[double-double]]s by a freshman in program history.{{cite web |last1=Stephens |first1=Brad |title=Bassey climbing up Hilltopper freshman record lists |url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/bassey-climbing-up-hilltopper-freshman-record-lists/article_2fa62486-9c4a-5ef7-999f-f347f6b3a1f5.html |website=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=January 25, 2019}} Bassey's sophomore season was cut short by a [[tibial plateau fracture]] he suffered against [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] that required surgery. Through 10 games, he was averaging 15.3 points, 9.2 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Western Kentucky's Charles Bassey out with tibia fracture |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28260966/western-kentucky-charles-bassey-tibia-fracture |access-date=December 10, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=December 9, 2019}} On November 26, 2020, Bassey recorded 21 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high seven blocks in a 75–69 win over [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].{{cite web |last1=MacDonald |first1=Jared |title=Bassey's Back: Hilltoppers beat Memphis to advance to Crossover Classic final |url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/basseys-back-hilltoppers-beat-memphis-to-advance-to-crossover-classic-final/article_fad7a38e-d7ae-55f8-930e-733cf7126d84.html |website=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]] |access-date=December 2, 2020 |date=November 26, 2020}} On December 10, he had a career-high 29 points and 14 rebounds in an 86–84 victory against [[Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball|Gardner–Webb]].{{cite web |last1=Kim |first1=David J. |title=Charles Bassey scores career-high 29 points, helps WKU escape Gardner-Webb with a win |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/12/10/western-kentucky-basketball-charles-bassey-career-high-fuels-win/3849277001/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=December 10, 2020}} At the close of the 2020–21 regular season, he was named the [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Conference USA Player of the Year]], while repeating as the league's Defensive Player of the Year. He averaged 17.6 points per game, 11.6 rebounds and 3.1 blocks per game.{{cite press release|url=https://conferenceusa.com/news/2021/3/9/mens-basketball-mbb-superlative-awards-announced.aspx|title=MBB: Superlative Awards Announced|publisher=[[Conference USA]] |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Western Kentucky center Charles Bassey entering 2021 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31177611/western-kentucky-center-charles-bassey-entering-2021-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=April 1, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]] | '''34''' || '''34''' || '''31.4''' || '''.627''' || '''.450''' || .769 || 10.0 || .7 || '''.8''' || 2.4 || 14.6 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]] | 10 || 10 || 28.1 || .533 || .167 || '''.787''' || 9.2 || '''1.3''' || '''.8''' || 1.6 || 15.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]] | 28 || 28 || 30.4 || .590 || .305 || .759 || '''11.6''' || .7 || .4 || '''3.1''' || '''17.6''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 72 || 72 || 30.5 || .596 || .319 || .768 || 10.5 || .8 || .6 || 2.6 || 15.9 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Shortly after arriving in the United States at age 14, Bassey's mother died. At the time, Bassey considered moving back to [[Nigeria]], but his father Akpan Ebong Bassey encouraged him to stay for financial reasons.{{cite web |title=Nike Hoop Summit, World Team notebook: Florida commit Andrew Nembhard is a wizard with the ball |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/hoop-summit/index.ssf/2018/04/nike_hoop_summit_world_team_no.html |publisher=[[OregonLive.com|OregonLive]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=April 11, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=St. Anthony coach wins custody battle over Bassey |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/article/St-Anthony-coach-wins-custody-battle-over-Bassey-11290027.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=July 14, 2017}} Canadian-born [[basketball]] coach, Hennssy Auriantal, who runs the Yes II Success organization that brings international players to American [[private school]]s, helped bring Bassey to the United States.{{cite web |last1=Klibanoff |first1=Eleanor |title=Louisville's Aspire Academy splits with partner school, controversial recruiter |url=https://wkuherald.com/sports/louisville-s-aspire-academy-splits-with-partner-school-controversial-recruiter/article_cf1f00f0-7629-11e8-a50a-9793d57e308e.html |website=[[College Heights Herald]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=June 22, 2018}} On March 31, 2017, Auriantal and his wife were granted [[conservatorship]] over Bassey. Bassey's father later filed a petition to reopen the case and give Nigerian basketball tournament organizer John Faniran custody over his son, but the petition was dropped due to lack of verification. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://wkusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/charles-bassey/2391 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers bio] {{Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bassey, Charles}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Nigerian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Nigerian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Lagos]] [[Category:Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball players]]
